policy.scope: source bytes, lexical structure, parsing, and rejection before semantic checking
policy.foreign_suffix: semantic checking, code generation, runtime, and foreign tools remain explicit downstream boundaries

claim.statement: For an identified UTF-8 source graph, the canonical Jet front end preserves source bytes and origins, consumes the complete input, builds the intended syntax, or returns a registered source diagnostic for the modeled rejection.
preconditions: The entry bytes and every imported source byte are identified by SHA-256.
The canonical Syntax.rs and syntax decision ledger are the only user-facing grammar authorities.
The production lexer and parser are the implementation under observation.
The compiler inspection command returns the versioned front-end value without a backend fallback.
A tool crash, timeout, signal, or malformed response is not an ordinary source rejection.
unsupported_cases: A missing or stale source witness
A parser or lexer output without exact source bytes
A source graph whose imported files are not identified
A source rejection without a registered diagnostic code and span
An unavailable compiler, tool crash, timeout, or malformed JSON response
A changed parser, lexer, grammar authority, source graph, or construction input

execution.crash_policy: tool failures are unavailable or invalid_oracle, never source rejection

binding_methods.implementation: crates/jet-lexer/src, crates/jet-parser/src, Source/Compiler.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs, and crates/jet-driver/src/Loader.rs
binding_methods.construction: the canonical compiler inspection seam and its exact-byte span invariants
binding_methods.limit: the finite source witnesses do not establish universal preservation

binding_methods.source: crates/jet-lexer/src, crates/jet-parser/src, Source/Compiler.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs, and crates/jet-driver/src/Loader.rs
binding_methods.candidate_binding: the recorded source implementation file set and compiler-proof identity
binding_methods.limit: the checker observes the production seam; it is not a mechanized theorem about all parser states

binding_methods.certificate: retained positive, negative, graph, scope, literal, and mutation source witnesses
binding_methods.limit: finite witnesses are evidence and cannot claim an unbounded proof

coverage.qualification_rule: Every source boundary row stays blocked unless an implementation-bound witness and current identity are present; no finite corpus claims universal proof.

proven: The checker validates the source contract, witness schema, identity fields, and obligation ownership.
The canonical inspection output is checked against exact source bytes, byte spans, graph descriptors, and registered diagnostics.
Tool failures, stale identities, malformed responses, discarded witnesses, and missing source boundaries cannot qualify as source proof.
assumed: The ratified Syntax.rs and syntax decision ledger state the intended Jet source law.
The production compiler inspection command reaches the same lexer, parser, loader, and diagnostic paths used by ordinary compilation.
The pinned jet.compiler-proof.v1 claim identifies the selected candidate toolchain.
tested: Positive precedence, scope, Unicode/literal, and imported-graph witnesses preserve their recorded source origins.
A malformed source witness yields its registered diagnostic rather than a checker or process failure.
An appended malformed suffix is retained as a mutation and cannot be silently discarded.
blocked: Universal preservation for every lexical, parsing, expansion, and source-graph input.
A fresh compiler replay or complete corpus qualification when the pinned compiler is unavailable.
Semantic checking, lowering, optimization, runtime, adapter, and foreign-tool preservation beyond this source boundary.
